verdict.reason: Both debates interact well and end knowing more than they began, but B introduces a rival reading of the 'behind' feeling (closeness with friends slipping) that changes another mind's advice and yields two readings with opposite observable predictions. That gives the user a more actionable conditional map. A's best move, that not-wanting can itself be borrowed, is sharp and directly relevant, but its ending converges on a looser blend of trials plus a suspicion check.

comparisons.a_observation: The Desire Detective argues that rejecting the milestones can be as borrowed as wanting them. The Realist concedes in A.debate[6] and pushes back on the 'suspicion spiral', which is a genuine exchange, though it ends in a fairly general synthesis.
comparisons.b_observation: The Experimenter's closeness reading makes the Desire Detective say it 'changes my advice'. The two readings predict opposite things (relief when apart versus relief when together), and B.debate[8] turns the experiment toward company rather than property.
comparisons.why_it_matters: The user can tell the two readings apart by watching their own reactions, and each points to a different action. A's narrowing is real but leaves the user with less to tell apart.

comparisons.a_observation: Takes the user's 'not sure I even want' seriously by questioning the doubt itself, not only the want.
comparisons.b_observation: Uses 'most of my friends' to suggest that the loss is shared ground and free evenings, not the houses. B.debate[10] and B.debate[11] also take seriously that 'not sure' can be a legitimate end state after trying.
comparisons.why_it_matters: Each debate draws a different, real implication from the user's own words, so neither clearly wins here.

comparisons.a_observation: Its branches turn on whether the pull survives privacy and whether the 'no' appears mainly around friends. Useful, but the actions are mostly 'trials' or 'stay the course'.
comparisons.b_observation: Its branches map to distinct actions: less exposure, investing in friendships, time-limited trials of a specific want, or accepting 'not sure'. Each has an observable trigger.
comparisons.why_it_matters: For a decision question, distinct actions tied to observable conditions are more usable than a general recommendation to experiment.

verdict.best_of_a: A.debate[5].text: The point that declaring you don't want the milestones can be reactive, 'keeps the crowd at the center', directly tests the user's uncertainty instead of taking it at face value.
verdict.best_of_b: B.debate[6].text: The Desire Detective accepts the closeness reading, revises its advice, and states the opposite predictions that would tell the two readings apart.

concerns.description: The situation summary and B.debate[4].text refer to 'the user' in the third person rather than addressing the reader, which reads less naturally.
'Ibarra notes that who we spend time with shapes who we become' loosely paraphrases Working Identity's theme of shifting connections. It is plausible, but the wording is not verified.
